title: certainty-scan: an evidence-sufficiency instrument for project work items
description:
A command-line instrument that scores each work item in an issue tracker on how much of the evidence that would justify confidence actually exists, and reports what is missing.

Five signals — validation (40), dependencies (20), acceptance criteria (15), evidence structure (15) and recorded decisions (10) — combine into a 0–100 certainty score per item. Scoring is a deterministic rule evaluation and performs no model inference, so a given backlog yields an identical report on every run.

Three anti-circularity rules prevent the tool, or the automation it measures, from raising its own score: machine-authored documentation is capped until a human confirms it, issues the tool files itself are excluded from later scoring, and relabelling an item as validated without linked evidence never earns full credit.

A sealed-reveal protocol (AES-256-GCM, key held by the researcher) supports blind comparison of machine scores against an independent project-manager rating, reported as a Spearman rank correlation.

The full instrument specification, including its stated limitations and the conditions that would falsify it, is published in the repository at docs/instrument-design.md.
